title: Naturality of the supported Hom identification under base change
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $h:T'\to T$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and
$i:D\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Choose schemes $D',V',V$
and maps $i':D'\hookrightarrow T'$, $h_D:D'\to D$, $v:V\hookrightarrow T$, $v':V'\hookrightarrow T'$
and $h_V:V'\to V$ such that $(h_D,i',i,h)$ and $(h_V,v',v,h)$ are pullback squares
[def-pc-fibre-product], and $V,V'$ are the open complements of $D,D'$.
Work in ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], using
inverse and direct image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and constant
sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. There are canonical restriction chain maps $q,q'$,
a canonical closed-immersion exchange $e:h^{-1}i_*A_D\to i'_*A_{D'}$, and natural cone
comparisons identifying the shifted restriction cones with derived Hom from the closed constant
sheaves [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]. The exchange is an isomorphism. For every bounded-below
complex $K$ of $A_T$-module sheaves and integer $q$, the induced relative-section pullback
$P_h$ satisfies
$$\Phi_{T',D',h^{-1}K}^q(P_h x)=
(h^{-1}\Phi_{T,D,K}^q(x))\circ e^{-1},$$
where $\Phi$ is the canonical supported-Hom identification. The same identifications make
forgetting support equal to precomposition by the constant unit $A_T\to i_*A_D$.
Here the constant coefficient, unit and exchange are the unrestricted helper constructions of [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class] and [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary]. On functorial degreewise-injective K-injective models I and J, the resolution comparison a:h^{-1}I→J extends the pulled-back resolution unit. The two section maps are section pullback followed by a; their diagonal shifted-cone map defines P_h. The supported Hom map sends c to a∘h^{-1}c∘e^{-1}. The cone comparison is normalized by the kernel inclusion c↦(0,c∘η), using evaluation at 1 to identify Hom(A_T,I) with global sections. Forgetting support is projection of this shifted cone to Γ(T,I), with that fixed target.

proof.text: Apply finite base change to the closed immersion i, which is finite, and compose with the canonical constant-sheaf isomorphism on D'. This is exactly supportedConstantExchange and is an isomorphism. The assumed closed immersion i' is used for the primed support sequence.

source.place: Tag 04FX; the closed-immersion case of finite base change

proof.text: The mate formula for exchange and naturality with respect to the constant-sheaf comparison identify the pulled-back constant unit with the primed unit. Compatibility of the constant-sheaf isomorphism with composition identifies the two routes around the pullback square. After inverting exchange, this gives the unit identity needed for precomposition on Hom.

source.place: Tags 03Q1 and 095L, adjunction formulas for inverse image and the constant unit

proof.text: Use the functorial degreewise injective K-injective replacement K→I and the fixed replacement h⁻¹K→J. Exact inverse image sends K→I to a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism. The right lifting property of J→0 against monomorphic quasi-isomorphisms supplies an actual chain map h⁻¹I→J extending the pulled-back resolution unit. This uses the construction of the existing replacement, without assuming that inverse image preserves injectives.

source.place: Tag 079P, the functorial fibrant replacement and its lifting property

proof.text: Apply Hom into an injective sheaf to the constant open-closed short exact sequence. The rank-one constant-sheaf/global-section linear equivalence identifies its first map with evaluation at 1 after precomposition by the specified constant unit, and its second map with the actual restriction of global sections. The adjunction for extension by zero identifies the third term with sections on the open complement. Apply the resulting normalized short exact sequence to each term of the chosen replacement. The kernel inclusion into the shifted restriction cone is a quasi-isomorphism. Localizing it and the canonical derived-functor computation on K-injective replacements constructs the normalized natural cone comparison, with the specified projection formulas.

source.place: Tags 095L and 0A45; the kernel-inclusion normalization of the support triangle

proof.text: Form the section chain maps from the natural pullback-of-sections transformations followed by the chosen resolution comparison. For the open component use the inverse of the square upper-star isomorphism. Functoriality of section pullback gives the restriction square. Form the Hom chain map by applying inverse image, precomposing with inverse exchange, and postcomposing with the comparison. Naturality of the rank-one section equivalence and the unit identity prove the square with the normalized kernel map. The two component projections of the mapping cone then prove that its diagonal map commutes with the kernel inclusion.

source.place: Tags 03Q1 and 0A45; blueprint supported Hom pullback compatibility

proof.text: Localize the strict square with the kernel inclusions, use the specified comparison isomorphisms, and apply the homology functor. Cancellation of these isomorphisms gives the stated pullback identity. The argument holds for all complexes and hence for the bounded-below complexes in the statement. For forgetting support, the cone projection composed with the kernel inclusion is exactly the normalized map to sections. Localizing this identity and applying homology gives both forgetting-support equations with the fixed section-complex target.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q149-3501975e4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, every cited node statement (with blueprint_updates), the full proof of lem-amb-closed-support-hom, unit sk-prop-sf-cbc, the main-20261015 blueprint texts lem-amb-closed-support-hom and lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map (the penultimate-paragraph sentence 'all cone maps … commute with pullback of the pair'), and Stacks 0A45, 04FX, 095L, 03Q1 and 08BJ. The statement is unchanged, the coefficient category is ordinary constant étale A-modules, and base change is ordinary inverse image with the underived closed exchange plus h_D^{-1}A_D=A_{D'}. Step checks: (1) the stalk identity on D' comes from the upperstar and lowerstar nodes; off D' both stalks are 0 by the direct-image formula, because h^{-1}D=D' as sets; conservativity finishes it. (2) The unit compatibility e∘h^{-1}η=η' holds on constant sections. (3) Resolutions are redone on T', so pullback is not assumed to preserve injectives. (4) The Hom sequence 0→C→E→B→0 is exact on the right by injectivity, and the counit formula makes the map restriction. (5) The 08BJ hypotheses are met: v_! is exact and left adjoint to v^{-1}. (6) I recomputed the sign of Cone(r)[-1] from def-weil-abstract-derived-category: d(b,s)=(-d_B b - r s, d_E s). Both lifts for the kernel-inclusion quasi-isomorphism are correct, and the normalization matches the parent's construction (c↦(0,c)) and the blueprint. (7) Both squares of chain maps commute strictly. (8) The cone homotopy (-s_B,s_E) is correct. (9) The derived reading of H^q(f_C) and the inverted ι give the formula. (10) Forgetting support is p∘ι=k=−∘η. Edge cases D=∅, D=T, h=id, h through V', A=0, K=0 and all q check out. A–F: one commit, no new nodes, proof_deps equals the union of the uses, all 12 off-unit statement tools are declared, and I accept them. Minor caveat, not a fault: step 6 fixes Φ to the parent's kernel-inclusion normalization, which the item's own statement calls canonical. Observation for the maintainer: the existing unsplit node lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback (Q128) contains an étale clause that is a special case of this item (A=A_{E,n}); it can cite this item when it is split. No fixes.

statement_change.old_statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $h:T'\to T$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $i':D'=T'\times_TD\hookrightarrow T'$ its scheme-theoretic pullback [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $V=T-D$ and $V'=T'-D'$. Work in ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], using inverse and direct image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The canonical closed-immersion exchange $e:h^{-1}i_*A_D\to i'_*A_{D'}$ is an isomorphism. For every bounded-below complex $K$ of $A_T$-module sheaves and integer $q$, in the abstract derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] put
$$H^q(T,V;K)=H^q(\operatorname{Cone}(R\Gamma(T,K)\to R\Gamma(V,K|_V))[-1]),$$
with etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Use the canonical supported-Hom identification [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] $\Phi_{T,D,K}^q:H^q(T,V;K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(i_*A_D,K[q])$. Then pullback $P_h$ on the relative section complexes satisfies
$$\Phi_{T',D',h^{-1}K}^q(P_h x)=(h^{-1}\Phi_{T,D,K}^q(x))\circ e^{-1}.$$
Here $P_h$ is induced by the canonical derived section pullback maps on $T$ and $V$, with their restriction-compatible comparison. The same identifications make forgetting support equal to precomposition by the constant unit $A_T\to i_*A_D$.
statement_change.what: The old statement left the complements and comparison maps implicit. The explicit formulation introduces their scheme maps and pullback squares and specifies the actual operations on K-injective representatives. The returned existential interface did not fix these operations: zero or rescaled maps could satisfy its equations. The repair fixes the exchange to the published mate, the resolution comparison to an extension of the resolution unit, the relative pullback to the diagonal cone map, the Hom pullback to inverse-image/precomposition, the cone isomorphism to the kernel-inclusion normalization, and forgetting support to projection to global sections. The additional dependencies supply already-published unrestricted constant/unit/exchange helpers; no finite coefficient or Cartier-divisor hypothesis is added.
